# Day in the Life of the Coherent Ecosystem 2026-05-21

## Narrative lens
These six days show oyatie as one coherent substrate, not as six suites and not as a bag of point products.
Every persona moves through multiple roles without changing the learned interaction grammar.
Every personal-to-work or work-to-personal transition is explicit because the same passkey identity is not permission to merge tenants.
Every story line is written as implementation guidance: if a future service cannot support the moment through shared identity, policy, workflow, ontology, audit, marketplace, UX, and compliance primitives, the service is not mature enough to claim ecosystem participation.
Front-office, middle-office, and back-office moments are described as pending ADR-0319 taxonomy projections over the same substrate, not as separate suites.

## Day 1 - Marcus
Marcus is modeled as engineering manager, parent, investor, employee, internal stakeholder, and personal consumer.
The narrative obligation is to show that role changes alter projection, not identity, policy engine, workflow engine, ontology, audit chain, or UX vocabulary.

### Day 1 08:00 personal Mail and family Calendar
Marcus enters personal Mail and family Calendar from the parent and household coordinator role projection inside the personal/family tenant context.
The visible products are Mail plus Calendar plus Messenger plus Notes, but the substrate path is still identity, tenancy, Cedar policy, Workflow Engine, Ontology projection, audit-chain, marketplace or settlement when money changes hands, and the shared UX shell vocabulary.
The risk focus is personal data must not leak to employer.
#### Day 1 08:00 personal Mail and family Calendar pass 1: scene, dialogue, and tenant gate
- Time anchor: 08:00 is captured as local-time event evt-d1-m01-p1-personal-mail-and- with day_index=1, persona=Marcus, role_projection=parent and household coordinator, and tenant_scope=personal/family.
- Dialogue: Marcus: "At 08:00, show me only the messages for this tenant."
- Visible surface: Mail plus Calendar plus Messenger plus Notes opens with tenant label, role label, data-class badge, and switch affordance before records render.
- First object: obj-d1-m01-p1-personal-mail-and- is created or reviewed with 6 linked records and no implicit copy from another tenant.
- Microservice handoff: mail receives the user intent, calendar normalizes the task state, and messenger pins the object reference.
- UX action: approve, assign, comment, attach evidence, route, defer, and review history keep the same button vocabulary as earlier moments.
- Risk guard: personal data must not leak to employer is shown as a blocking banner when the shell detects stale projection cache or mixed-tenant evidence.
- Concrete value: amount_or_count=8891, related_items=6, projection_cache_age_ms=118, and audit_subject=obj-d1-m01-p1-personal-mail-and-.
- Role result: Marcus stays one passkey-backed human while the active projection changes the allowed object set.
- Stop condition: the moment cannot complete until Cedar allow, workflow run id, ontology node id, and audit event id are all visible.
- Accessibility path: keyboard focus lands on the tenant switcher first, then the primary task, then evidence review.
- No-training proof: the shell does not introduce a new SaaS grammar; it narrows the familiar commands to parent and household coordinator.
- Validation fixture: day1-0800-personal-mail-and-family-calendar-p1 asserts dialogue, object id, data value, microservice handoff, Cedar decision, workflow id, ontology node, and audit seal are all present.
- Handoff contract: personal intent must traverse workflow-engine -> ontology -> audit-chain with evidence_ref=evi-1344 before the user sees done.
- Reviewer check: replay personal Mail and family Calendar pass 1 and confirm tenant label, role projection, denial or approval copy, recovery behavior, and metric sample 347 are visible together.

#### Day 1 08:00 personal Mail and family Calendar pass 2: object graph and concrete values
- Object graph: obj-d1-m01-p2-personal-mail-and- links person:marcus, tenant:personal-family, role:parent-and-household-coordinator, workflow_run:wf-1059, and evidence:evi-1059.
- Data values: source_row_count=17, delta_window_minutes=24, retention_class=tenant-scoped, and data_class=INTERNAL.
- Dialogue checkpoint: Marcus says "show the source values before the projection writes anything."
- Microservice handoff: mail emits command cmd-1059; workflow-engine opens wf-1059; ontology stores normalized node on projection rev p1.1.2.
- Named fields: tenant_id, role_projection_id, source_object_ref, workflow_run_id, policy_version, and audit_chain_ref are mandatory.
- Relationship edges: owner, participant, evidence_for, routed_by, and supersedes are resolved before the UX shows completion.
- Tenant split: personal/family records and employer or agency records keep separate object ids even when the same human appears in both.
- Concrete sample: D1-M01-P2-personal-mail-and--A imports 17 rows, D1-M01-P2-personal-mail-and--B rejects 1 stale cross-tenant reference, and D1-M01-P2-personal-mail-and--C waits for evidence seal.
- Conflict behavior: duplicate people, duplicate files, or duplicate cases merge only through tenant-approved identity resolution.
- Review path: the object inspector shows original value, normalized value, policy decision, and workflow branch side by side.
- Export rule: CSV/JSON export is disabled until the audit-chain event contains the exact tenant and role projection.
- Result: the story gains data density through named records, values, edges, and owners instead of a generic substrate claim.
- Validation fixture: day1-0800-personal-mail-and-family-calendar-p2 asserts dialogue, object id, data value, microservice handoff, Cedar decision, workflow id, ontology node, and audit seal are all present.
- Handoff contract: personal intent must traverse workflow-engine -> ontology -> audit-chain with evidence_ref=evi-1457 before the user sees done.
- Reviewer check: replay personal Mail and family Calendar pass 2 and confirm tenant label, role projection, denial or approval copy, recovery behavior, and metric sample 460 are visible together.

#### Day 1 08:00 personal Mail and family Calendar pass 3: policy decision and workflow handoff
- Cedar request: principal=marcus, action=mail.execute, resource=obj-d1-m01-p3-personal-mail-and-, context={tenant:personal-family, role:parent-and-household-coordinator, purpose:personal-mail-and-family-calendar}.
- Policy outcome: allow requires tenant membership, role purpose, data-class match, device posture, jurisdiction pack, and emergency override=false.
- Dialogue checkpoint: Marcus says "if policy denies it, show me the reason and keep the workflow paused."
- Microservice handoff: cedar-policy returns decision dec-1070; workflow-engine chooses branch br-8; audit-chain records policy_version pv-1-1.
- Workflow state: queued -> policy_checked -> object_projected -> evidence_attached -> user_confirmed, with SLA timer 140ms for visible feedback.
- Exception path: if personal data must not leak to employer, the workflow routes to supervisor_review rather than falling back to cached data.
- Approval values: approver_count=3, escalation_after_minutes=50, evidence_items=28, rollback_checkpoint=rb-1070.
- Tenant boundary: the policy response includes denied_fields when the role can see the record shell but not the sensitive payload.
- Handoff proof: calendar cannot mutate until workflow-engine stores the Cedar decision id and ontology projection id together.
- Recovery: failed connector reads surface retry, quarantine, or manual evidence attach; silent success is not allowed.
- Audit event: EVT-DAY-LIFE-POLICY-HANDOFF carries actor, action, resource, decision, and workflow_run_ref.
- Result: the user experiences one workflow language while each service proves its own authorization boundary.
- Validation fixture: day1-0800-personal-mail-and-family-calendar-p3 asserts dialogue, object id, data value, microservice handoff, Cedar decision, workflow id, ontology node, and audit seal are all present.
- Handoff contract: personal intent must traverse workflow-engine -> ontology -> audit-chain with evidence_ref=evi-1570 before the user sees done.
- Reviewer check: replay personal Mail and family Calendar pass 3 and confirm tenant label, role projection, denial or approval copy, recovery behavior, and metric sample 573 are visible together.

#### Day 1 08:00 personal Mail and family Calendar pass 4: UX surface and recovery behavior
- UX surface: the task opens as personal mail and family calendar with primary action, evidence drawer, tenant switcher, and history rail.
- Dialogue checkpoint: Marcus says "put the risky field behind review, but let me finish the safe part now."
- Microservice handoff: mail renders the view model, calendar owns durable state, messenger resolves object labels, and audit-chain seals user-visible errors.
- Concrete UI data: badge=personal-family, queue_position=3, pending_items=10, last_sync_ms=151, and recovery_code=ux-1081.
- Recovery behavior: stale cache clears with a visible reason, preserves draft text, blocks export, and asks for explicit tenant re-selection.
- Accessibility detail: screen-reader announces tenant, role, data class, decision, and next action before reading the record body.
- Mobile/offline path: offline edits are drafts only; sync requires policy replay and duplicate detection before any server write.
- Training-transfer detail: the same approve/comment/route/history controls appear whether the surface is Mail plus Calendar plus Messenger plus Notes.
- Failure copy: the denial names personal data must not leak to employer, the service boundary, and the evidence id instead of telling the user to try another product.
- Operator shortcut: command palette action route-evidence:personal-mail-and-family-calendar maps to the same workflow branch as the button.
- Visual boundary: personal, employer, agency, healthcare, and side-business tenants use labels plus data-class badges, not separate mental models.
- Result: the UX is bespoke to the moment while the command grammar stays coherent.
- Validation fixture: day1-0800-personal-mail-and-family-calendar-p4 asserts dialogue, object id, data value, microservice handoff, Cedar decision, workflow id, ontology node, and audit seal are all present.
- Handoff contract: personal intent must traverse workflow-engine -> ontology -> audit-chain with evidence_ref=evi-1683 before the user sees done.

#### Day 1 08:00 personal Mail and family Calendar pass 5: audit, observability, and evidence
- Audit event: EVT-DAY-LIFE-EVIDENCE sealed at 08:00 for obj-d1-m01-p5-personal-mail-and- with actor=Marcus, tenant=personal-family, role=parent-and-household-coordinator, and workflow=wf-1092.
- Observability values: policy_latency_ms=162, projection_cache_age_ms=185, workflow_queue_age_s=12, audit_seal_lag_ms=92.
- Dialogue checkpoint: Marcus says "I need the proof trail before I hand this to someone else."
- Microservice handoff: mail emits domain event ev-1092; audit-chain signs hash h00000444; observability records service span span-personal-mail-and-family-calendar.
- Evidence payload: includes before_value, after_value, policy_decision_id, workflow_branch, ontology_node_ref, user_visible_message, and rollback_checkpoint.
- Alert threshold: if audit seal lag exceeds 392ms, the shell marks the action pending and prevents export.
- Data sample: 21 evidence attachments, 1 approvers, 2 denied fields, and $639 equivalent business impact when money is involved.
- Compliance pack: tenant policy chooses HIPAA, SOX, EU AI Act, labor, family, or consumer pack from context rather than from product name.
- Review screen: history rail groups policy, workflow, ontology, and audit rows under one timestamp instead of four tool logs.
- Incident proof: support can replay wf-1092 without reading payload fields outside its role.
- Retention: evidence keeps source ids and normalized ids so deletion, legal hold, and export can be proved later.
- Result: every moment carries operational proof, not a story-only assertion.
- Validation fixture: day1-0800-personal-mail-and-family-calendar-p5 asserts dialogue, object id, data value, microservice handoff, Cedar decision, workflow id, ontology node, and audit seal are all present.
- Handoff contract: personal intent must traverse workflow-engine -> ontology -> audit-chain with evidence_ref=evi-1796 before the user sees done.
- Reviewer check: replay personal Mail and family Calendar pass 5 and confirm tenant label, role projection, denial or approval copy, recovery behavior, and metric sample 799 are visible together.

#### Day 1 08:00 personal Mail and family Calendar pass 6: outcome, boundary proof, and transfer
- Completed outcome: Marcus finishes personal Mail and family Calendar at 08:00 with workflow wf-1103, ontology node obj-d1-m01-p6-personal-mail-and-, and audit seal evi-1103.
- Dialogue checkpoint: Marcus says "this feels like the same system, but the data stayed in the right place."
- Microservice handoff: mail returns user-facing completion, workflow-engine stores terminal state, ontology keeps the normalized graph, and audit-chain closes evidence.
- Boundary proof: personal data must not leak to employer is handled by tenant_id, role_projection_id, data_class, policy_version, and visible denial copy.
- Transfer proof: the next persona can reuse approve, assign, comment, attach evidence, route, defer, escalate, and review history without product retraining.
- Concrete result values: closed_items=3, minutes_saved=28, denied_leaks=3, evidence_refs=9, rollback_checkpoint=rb-1103.
- Personal/work split: the same passkey subject never implies shared data; only tenant membership and role projection unlock views.
- Marketplace/settlement: if the moment created a commercial obligation, DealSet ds-1103 carries counterparty, tax, receipt, and refund state.
- Compliance close: the pack can explain why the moment was allowed, denied, exported, retained, or deleted.
- Residual risk: adapter drift, stale object labels, or missing evidence blocks the capability claim until validation catches up.
- Re-entry: returning to this moment later starts from wf-1103 and not from browser memory or a vendor-specific inbox.
- Result: the arc is concrete enough to test as service handoffs rather than a generic ecosystem slogan.
- Validation fixture: day1-0800-personal-mail-and-family-calendar-p6 asserts dialogue, object id, data value, microservice handoff, Cedar decision, workflow id, ontology node, and audit seal are all present.
- Handoff contract: personal intent must traverse workflow-engine -> ontology -> audit-chain with evidence_ref=evi-1909 before the user sees done.
- Reviewer check: replay personal Mail and family Calendar pass 6 and confirm tenant label, role projection, denial or approval copy, recovery behavior, and metric sample 912 are visible together.
